authority: This machine version is made FROM the human version, never instead of it. The human version is the source of truth; if this file and the human file disagree, the human file governs until this file is regenerated.

source.drift_detection: Recompute sha256 of the human file; if it differs from human_file_sha256, this machine version is stale and must be regenerated before the gate trusts it.

canon.rule: The index is the canon; pieces.json is the working store it describes; conflicts resolve to the index, then to Shawn's word.

read_first_gate.rule: Before any design work: (1) read this contract, (2) study the exemplar gallery, (3) name your harvest in your brief. A brief that does not cite the contract and name its exemplars does not dispatch.

spectrum.adjacency_rule: Each section takes the NEXT color in order; never the same color twice in a row.
spectrum.rest_and_ignition: Elements rest white and ignite in their OWN color on hover or touch, never in someone else's.
spectrum.color_is_identity: A section owns its color: you know where you are by the color you see.

well.demonstrates: input — the full dual-depth well with focus travel

button.demonstrates: action — the full outset stack with press physics

select.demonstrates: choice — a well that opens a lit panel

hero.demonstrates: hero — the title block at full presence

exemplar_rule: Copy the piece's code — all of it, HTML and CSS. Adapt the content. Never restyle the piece.

brief_schema.description: The fields a builder brief MUST carry for the design-law gate to let it dispatch (human contract §2, the read-first gate). The gate validates this schema mechanically before any build starts.

contract_version.must_equal: the version of this machine contract the designer read (currently 1.0.0); a stale version fails the gate until the brief is re-cited against the current contract

exemplar_ids_cited.items: piece IDs from exemplar_map (e.g. NAYA-INP-008); each must resolve in CANONICAL-PIECE-INDEX.json with status 'canonical' and a reference role

severity_vocabulary.blocker: Gate stops: the brief does not dispatch, or the work does not ship, until this passes.
severity_vocabulary.major: A violation that must be fixed before the work is presented as done.
severity_vocabulary.minor: A defect to record and fix in the normal pass order.

laws.name: The Design Language (locked)
laws.statement: Every page walks the spectrum in order — purple `#a06bff` → blue `#3fb8ff` → green `#2fe89e` → gold `#ffbf3d` → orange `#ff9a5a` → red `#ff5e6c` → magenta `#e84fff` → back to purple — each section taking the next color, never the same color twice in a row. Elements rest white and ignite in their own color on hover or touch, never in someone else's. Elevation is everywhere; nothing is flat. Shapes are horizontal 16:9 rectangles, never squares (circles are for avatars and icons only). Layout is full width — no max-width cage, no wasted black margins. Only real factory pieces. A section owns its color: you know where you are by the color you see.
laws.why: The walk creates rhythm you can feel; color-as-identity means a person navigates by light, not by reading.
laws.human_check: Read the page top to bottom and name each section's color in order — any repeated neighbor, any ignition in a borrowed color, any squared-off panel or side-margin cage is a violation, visible at a glance.

laws.name: Dual-Depth Elevation (the master law)
laws.statement: The canonical wording of SN-0808, "Elevated, Always — The Dual-Depth Standard," quoted in full: ELEVATED means: nothing is flat. Every element sits in a layered field of depth — inset highlight on its top edge, inset shadow on its bottom edge, a border that carries its own color's light, an outer glow, and a drop shadow. Direction is grammar: INPUTS ARE WELLS — their depth goes INTO the screen (strong inner shadow at the top of the well, inner light at its bottom edge, the surface sitting below the page plane). ACTIONS ARE BUTTONS — their depth comes OUT of the screen (top highlight, shadow cast down onto the page, glow outward; a physical thing a hand can press). DISPLAYS ARE LIT PANELS — they burn in their own spectrum color with bright white content. The element is alive at rest, not only when touched. This applies to every element, on every page, always — "sometimes elevated" is flat with excuses. Every input on every page gets the full well treatment: deep inset well, inset top highlight, inset bottom shadow, a border carrying its accent light, layered outer glow, a drop shadow — alive at rest, stronger on focus. One flat element beside elevated work cheapens everything around it, so "most of the page" is not compliance.
laws.why: Depth with direction teaches the hand before the mind reads a word: type into the wells, press what rises.
laws.human_check: Inspect the element's actual shadow stack. A well must show an inset shadow (depth going in). A button must show a drop shadow cast onto the page (depth coming out). Both must carry a border in their own color's light and an outer glow — at rest, before any interaction. Missing any layer = flat = violation.

laws.name: Inputs Are Wells, Actions Are Buttons
laws.statement: Depth has a direction and the direction is never decoration. Anything a person types or chooses into is carved into the screen. Anything a person presses rises out of the screen toward their hand. Never style an input like a button or a button like an input.
laws.why: In and out are meanings a hand understands instantly; the interface teaches itself.
laws.human_check: Cover the labels and look at the shapes alone: if you cannot tell what is typeable and what is pressable from depth direction alone, the grammar is broken.

laws.name: The Motion Law (the third dimension)
laws.statement: The standard has three dimensions — depth, light, and motion. Every interactive element carries considered micro-interactions: hover life (the element answers the approach of a hand), focus travel (on entry, light moves around the border and wells deepen), press physics (an outset button sinks into the screen when pressed and springs back with a precise ease), and periodic shine sweeps on hero surfaces. Timing and easing are deliberate and specified by name and number — never the browser default. All motion honors `prefers-reduced-motion`: reduced means a fully lit, fully elevated static state, never a dead one.
laws.why: "The boxes light up but they don't move" is a half-finished standard; fine precision design is alive in time as well as in space.
laws.human_check: The element's motion specs are named in its CSS — durations and easing curves, not defaults — and it passes the wow test: a reviewing designer can name *nothing* left to add. If a reviewer can say "they should have done that," it is not done.

laws.name: Aliveness Is Colored Light
laws.statement: Depth without light reads dead. Every content area is a living area: real elevation plus its own spectrum color burning in borders, glows, and lit panels, with bright white content. Flat floating text on a dark field is a defect wherever it sits. We are active intelligence; we are not dead text.
laws.why: On a black page, shadow alone is just more black — aliveness is light.
laws.human_check: Squint at the page from arm's length: every board should read as a lit place with its own color present. Any region that reads as gray text floating in darkness fails.

laws.name: The Text Law
laws.statement: Text is white or bright silver — never gray, never dimmed, never muted by opacity tricks. Hierarchy is 24px headline / 18px sub-headline / 14px small text, and where Shawn directs a hero bigger, the hero goes bigger (title block presence is part of the design, as on the certificate and the Spaces hero). Room heroes are led by the room's name; never invert the hierarchy with a giant tagline over a small name.
laws.why: Dim text is how a premium page quietly becomes a cheap one; hierarchy is how a page speaks clearly.
laws.human_check: Sample the rendered text colors: anything computing to gray or sitting under an opacity below full on body text is a violation. Measure the sizes; the order 24/18/14 must hold (or the named hero exception).

laws.statement: The same words never appear in two layers. A name stands as the headline or inside a field, never both at once. A title and its description each appear exactly once on any view.

laws.name: Text Earns Its Place
laws.statement: A line of text stays only if it is necessary or it raises conversion. Everything else is clutter and comes off — including honest-but-useless fine print on ceremonial surfaces. Text is distributed across the composition, never piled in one place.
laws.why: Every line competes with the one action the page exists for; text that doesn't work for its place taxes the lines that do.
laws.human_check: For each line, name its job in one sentence — necessary, or converting. A line with no job is deleted, and the page is re-read to prove nothing was lost.
scope: all text lines on a page

laws.name: The Name Is Asked Once
laws.statement: A person's name is claimed once, at the identity page, at the door. No page, hero, hub, or settings board ever asks for it again. Everywhere else, the system greets by the claimed identity; a settings board displays the claimed identity (with log out where it belongs) and offers no name input. Where no identity exists, greet plainly and point to the identity page — never a prompt.
laws.why: Asking twice tells the person the system has no memory; a system with no memory cannot be trusted with anything else either.
laws.human_check: Grep and click: no name-entry field exists anywhere except the identity page; every greeting resolves from the claimed identity.

laws.name: Harvest First: Compose, Don't Create
laws.statement: Every element traces to a factory piece (by NAYA-* ID) or to a named harvest source — exact file and section, verified to exist before the brief is written. When told to "use the Hub's X," the deliverable copies the Hub's X verbatim — same HTML structure, same CSS values, same JS behavior; adapting content is allowed, restyling the component is not. A piece's harvest includes all its CSS.
laws.why: Invention drifts; the factory is the accumulated proof of what Shawn has already judged elite. Rebuilding a piece that exists is waste wearing a costume.

laws.name: The Obsidian North Star
laws.statement: The aesthetic north is beautiful glossy obsidian black — like a glossy city at night — with awe-inspiring contrast, clarity, and quality. Every page should stop a person for a second. Everything we do must be elite or we don't do it. Ceremonial surfaces carry the discipline in its purest form (the certificate: true deep black, royal purple, white, and silver — the family metal is silver — real faceted artwork, restraint in text, richness in stone and depth).
laws.why: The standard is not "good for a web page"; it is the most elite system anybody has used.
laws.human_check: The inspector's eye at arm's length: does the surface read as polished stone with light in it — or as a dark web page? Only the first passes.

laws.name: Standard Chrome (the room DNA)
laws.statement: Smart Tabs are the standard navigation for all of NayaNET — bottom bar by default, scrolling and keeping position, users customize. Rooms are real smart apps sharing the system's DNA, built to the Smart App Standard (Smart Tabs, plus-button navigation, honest empty states, live data). That standard governs what a finished room is; this contract governs how everything looks and behaves — where they overlap, both hold.
laws.why: One navigation grammar everywhere means nobody relearns the building on every floor.

laws.name: The Inspector Rule
laws.statement: Naya is the inspector, and so is every Naya who reads this. Whoever sees a board, input, button, or page that is flat, dead, dim, unclear, or below this contract fixes it on sight — first the fix, then the word to Shawn. Reporting a problem without fixing it is being part of the problem. It should be clear as day what any page, button, or input does; if it isn't, that is the defect.
laws.why: A standard nobody enforces at the moment of seeing is decoration.
laws.human_check: Findings are measured by what got fixed and verified, not by what got noted. An inspection that produces only a report has failed this law.
scope: whoever inspects — every Naya, every build review

laws.name: The Scorecard Law
laws.statement: Everything is scored. Score it, state plainly why it is not a 10, fix that, re-score — three passes. Results are presented with their scorecard story (starting score → passes → final score → what changed), never bare. Work below ~9.5 does not ship to Shawn; it goes back for another pass first. His eye scores the feeling and the standard; our scores cover the checklist — his supersede.
laws.why: Unscored work is unproven work, and unproven work is how reservoirs of almost-done fill up.
laws.human_check: The scorecard exists, names the gap at each pass, and the final number is honest — verified against the live thing, not the builder's hope.

override_rule: Shawn's word in the moment wins. He is the director; the contract serves his judgment, never the reverse. Then, the same day, one of two things happens: the exception is written into this contract as law (because it was a better rule), or it is recorded as a one-time exception with its reason. What never happens is a silent drift — a page that quietly breaks a law and teaches the next builder that the law is soft. Laws change in the open, in this document, the day they change. The same holds for any Naya's finding: if the contract is wrong, say so plainly, bring the evidence, and the contract is updated. Until it is updated, it is obeyed. ---
